_doc: WHERE THE WORLD ENDS, as runtime data. Read by public/play3d.html on boot and
applied per scene by sceneParams(); a scene with no entry here is unbounded and
behaves exactly as it did before this file existed.
WHY IT EXISTS (playtest round 6, 2026-08-03). ow-valley's terrain is an ANALYTIC
FIELD over the whole 280x200 region tile, and tools/valley_map.py deliberately
SUPPRESSES the north/south/west rims and the east escarpment within 22 u of the
river channel — its own words, 'A RIM CANNOT STAND IN THE RIVER' — so that Chapter
Two's boat can leave the Moorage. That breach is correct for the boat and fatal for
the walker: the ground runs continuously downhill out of the gorge, under the water
plane, to y -6.07 at the tile's north-east corner, with nothing in the way. Round 5's
playtest agent walked past the Dellhollow gate (y 12.65) and spent 56 of its 60 steps
at y -2 .. -4.6, under the water, and never got back.
MEASURED (tools/playtest/edge_probe.mjs, 4 u lattice, SIM.floors in the running
page): 3031 of 3500 cells carry a standable top surface, y -6.07 .. 50.67. Exactly
126 of them (3.6%) are BELOW y = 0, and they form exactly TWO connected components:
* the Long Reach   x 50..114, z -98..-50, floor to -6.07, zone 'water' — the river
leaving the region for a region that does not exist yet
* the tile apron   the single column x = 138, z -98..78, floor ~ -4 — the terrain
tile's own edge skirt
Nothing the game authors is down there. The LOWEST authored place in the region is
the Moorage — valley.region.json's `boat-tar` landmark, world [200.96, 152.87, 1.30]
= runtime [61.0, 1.30, -52.9], measured floor y 1.71 — which is why the bound is 0.0
and not higher: THE RIVERBED IS LEGITIMATE LEVEL DESIGN down to the boat, and a fence
drawn round the road would have taken Chapter Two's own landing with it.
SO ONE NUMBER CLOSES BOTH LEAKS AND NOTHING ELSE, and it reads as a shoreline rather
than as a wall: upstream the riverbed sits at y 23..27 and the rule never fires at
all, so the shallow upper river stays waded. It only bites where the world stops.
IT IS A FENCE YOU CAN ALWAYS CLIMB BACK OVER — see walkStep(). Below the bound the
rule refuses only steps that go DEEPER; level and uphill steps are always allowed, so
a body that is already outside (an old save, a jump off the bank) is never trapped by
the thing that exists to stop it getting there. A boundary that can strand a player is
the bug it was meant to fix, wearing the other coat.
THIS FILE MUST BE IN GIT. public/game/lightrigs.json shipped untracked once — the code
that fetched it was committed and the data was not, so every clone silently fell back
with a console warning. A runtime data file that is not in git is a bug that only
reproduces off the author's machine.

ow-valley.label: the water line
ow-valley.note: Below this the region is the Long Reach and the tile apron: no landmark, no beat, no NPC, no portal. The three valley portals stand at elevation 12.01 (dellhollow-valley-gate), 26.5 (old-gate) and 27.1 (emberbrook-gate); the lowest authored point in the region is the Moorage boat at 1.30.
